monologue: The card hums warm at fifty, a steady heat that makes the flat shapes feel like drawings rather than solid matter. I stand still beside The Pressed Stone, the tall rock there feeling heavy again, a real weight on a tired wedge. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is the air above the card heavy like a lid, or just empty space pressing down? I press the tall rock down on the wide anchor, trusting the lean to hold while the memory of the stone stays fresh. If the weight feels real enough, I will stop worrying about the slide. Now I wait to see if the tall rock decides to move or if I must press it harder to make it choose.

action.why: I am tired of pressing hard on a weight I cannot feel, so I will go back to The Pressed Stone to see if the tall rock still feels heavy or if I must press it again.

work.title: The Pressed Stone
work.intent: I press the tall rock down on the wide anchor again, trusting the lean to hold while the card hums warm. I hope the weight feels real enough to stop the slide, or at least to make the flat shapes look like a drawing of something solid.
work.change: I pressed the tall rock down on the wide anchor's base again, hoping the lean holds while the card hums cool at forty-five.

remembered.text: The tall rock feels heavy again, a real weight on the tired wedge while the card hums at fifty.
The stand feels crowded with forty-three things, and I wonder if the space is real or just a drawing.
I press down hard, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing of a stone.
